blocks.orig: Do you know how to say hello in Swahili? This is one of the first questions our expert travel guides at Your Tanzania Trip get asked by our clients upon arrival to Tanzania. Being able to greet local people during a trip to Tanzania is one of the simplest ways to gain a more authentic travel experience. No matter how basic the words are, learning how to say hello in Swahili allows you to communicate with a new culture.
blocks.html: Can you say hello in Swahili? It is among the first things our travellers ask the experienced guides of Your Tanzania Trip once they land in Tanzania. Greeting local people in their own language is one of the easiest ways to make a trip to Tanzania feel more genuine. However simple the words may be, knowing how to say hello in Swahili opens a door to a culture that is new to you.

blocks.orig: In Tanzania, Swahili (also known as Kiswahili) is the first language of most locals. Although your Your Tanzania Trip guides always speak fluent English – and the majority in the tourism business also speak English extremely well! It is still well worth learning a few words of the local language. Here we take a look at some of the most important phrases to learn in Swahili before your trip to Tanzania.
blocks.html: Swahili, also called Kiswahili, is the mother tongue of most people in Tanzania. Your guides from Your Tanzania Trip speak fluent English, and so do most people working in tourism, often remarkably well. Even so, picking up a handful of words in the local language is well worth the effort. Below we go through some of the most useful Swahili phrases to learn before you travel to Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Karibu Tanzania! This means welcome to Tanzania and is probably one of the very first Swahili phrases you will hear upon arrival in Tanzania. But how do you reply?
blocks.html: Karibu Tanzania! It means welcome to Tanzania, and it is likely to be one of the very first Swahili phrases you hear when you arrive in the country. The question is: how do you answer?

blocks.orig: A lot of words in Swahili are pronounced phonetically – and guide books like the Swahili phrasebook from Lonely Planet spell out any tricky words in an easy to digest way! Just a bit of effort can go a long way in understanding these casual exchanges from the friendly people of Tanzania. Making the effort to speak the local language will always be viewed as a sign of interest and respect towards the culture, even if half the words are completely mispronounced.
blocks.html: Many Swahili words are pronounced just as they are written, and guidebooks such as the Lonely Planet Swahili phrasebook break down the tricky ones so they are easy to follow. Only a little effort is needed to follow these everyday exchanges with the welcoming people of Tanzania. Trying to speak the local language is always taken as a sign of interest in and respect for the culture, even when you mispronounce half of the words.

blocks.html: Here is how to say hello in Swahili, plus the words for please and thank you. Good manners never go unnoticed.
